The US and other western countries have exactly zero manufacturing advantage borne of automation/robotics. The same robots used in our facilities are used as much if not more in China, India, the Philippines etc. The big players (Fanuc, Kawasaki, Yaskawa) are all Japanese, with only a few others (Kuka - likely soon to be aquired by the Chinese, and ABB) made in Europe.

Manufacturing equipment (CNC machines) are mainly made in Korea and Taiwan, with high end machines made in Japan and Europe. The US has one domestically owned manufacturer of CNC machines, Haas, that are generally considered inferior and rarely used outside the US. Some of the Japanese brands (Mazak) have facilities inside the US to serve the US market.

Because none of this stuff is American owned or made in the US, the government have no power to exercise export sanctions to less developed countries, and therefore no power to stop them competing globally, which is exactly how they built up the huge technology gap of the previous century.
